# My Thinking

I have about 15 mu of contracted land, flat and loamy, here on the North China Plain. My father farmed this same land, and I have been farming it since I was a teenager. There is really only one way to farm here: winter wheat followed by summer maize. Every household in the village does it. I know these two crops well. I do not need to experiment.

For wheat, I will buy improved seeds from the village supply cooperative — probably Kenong 199 or Shi 4366, whatever they have in stock. These varieties do well in our soil. I do not risk trying something new. For corn, I always buy hybrid seeds, same as my neighbors. The hybrid yields more, and I have seen that with my own eyes over many years.

Fertilizer — I put enough, maybe a little more than enough. Better to ensure the crop has what it needs. I broadcast compound fertilizer before sowing wheat, then top-dress urea at jointing. For corn, I do the same basic approach. I have been doing this for twenty years and the yields are steady.

For water, wheat needs three irrigations here in Quzhou — at sowing if the soil is dry, once over winter, and once at jointing or heading in spring. Corn grows in the rainy season so I usually only need one pump if summer is dry.

I spray herbicide on the wheat after emergence, then fungicide and aphid spray before it heads. For corn, I spray once for weeds and once for borer. That is standard.

I till the ground with the rotary machine before wheat sowing. For corn, I plant directly into the wheat stubble after the combine goes through — saves time and diesel.
